pages.x: For two centuries seven kingdoms fought over the old lands of the Zhou kings, with armies of hundreds of thousands of conscripted farmers armed with iron and crossbows. It was also an age of thinkers: followers of Confucius, the Daoists, and the general Sun Tzu, whose Art of War is still read.

Qin, in the far west, was remade by the minister Shang Yang into a state built for war. Families were grouped in fives and punished for each other's crimes, rank came only from service in war, and soldiers were rewarded by the number of enemy heads they brought back.

In 260 BC Qin trapped the army of Zhao at Changping. After 46 days the starving Zhao soldiers surrendered, and the Qin general Bai Qi had almost all of them killed, by tradition 400,000 men. Zhao never recovered.

In 227 BC the prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to kill the king of Qin. He came with a gift, a map of land to be handed over, with a poisoned dagger rolled up inside. As the map unrolled he seized the king's sleeve and stabbed, and missed. The king ran round a pillar, finally drew his long sword and cut him down.

Between 230 and 221 BC Qin conquered the other six kingdoms one by one. Its king took a new title, Shi Huangdi, the First Emperor. He made everyone use the same script, coins and weights, and even the same width of cart axle, so that wagons fitted the ruts of every road.

The emperor had older walls joined into one long wall against the nomads of the north, and built thousands of kilometres of roads and canals. Hundreds of thousands of conscripts did the work, and many died.
pages.fx: It was the first Great Wall. Most of the wall standing today was built much later, by the Ming, but the idea began with Qin.

pages.x: Near his tomb the First Emperor was buried with more than 7,000 life-size clay soldiers, each with its own face, and horses and chariots. Farmers digging a well found them in 1974. His burial mound itself has never been opened.

The Qin dynasty fell only 15 years after unification, but China never again stayed divided for long. The emperor, the single script and the central government Qin made lasted 2,000 years, and the name China may come from Qin.
pts: Ended the Warring States in 221 BC
Gave China one script, one coinage, one measure
Began the Great Wall and the terracotta army
